Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the draft order form. Our procurement team dug into Exhibit A (pricing schedule) and flagged a potential operational ambiguity in the fallback workflow tied to the cap/floor safeguards. Specifically:

- Section 3.2 (Fallback to alternate model variants) appears to permit Redwood to route traffic to a lower-cost model which the order form then treats as the new pricing baseline for the subsequent quarter. That change would reduce the cap but also seems to remove the original floor protection.
- We need to understand: if Redwood triggers an automatic fallback for capacity reasons, does Acme retain the original floor for true-ups, or does the fallback snapshot the floor/cap at the moment of fallback?

This matters operationally because our finance team uses the floor to plan committed spend and the cap to estimate upper bound exposure. If the fallback can silently change the floor, it creates a revenue recognition and budgeting issue for us.

Can you send an updated redline that: (a) clarifies whether floor values are preserved across fallback events, and (b) adds an explicit notification and approval window before any floor change takes effect? Procurement would prefer a 10-business-day notification and a right to reject a floor change that materially (>10%) reduces the guaranteed minimum.

Appreciate a quick turn — we are targeting internal approval next Thursday.

Best,
Liam

Karthik / Sofia — draft redline below. I focused on clarity and an operationally enforceable process. Inline markers show "[REDACTED]" placeholders for numeric thresholds that we can finalize with Acme.

--- Exhibit A, Pricing Schedule — new subsection 3.2.1 (Fallback and Pricing Protections) ---

- Original: "If Redwood elects to route Customer traffic to a compatible model variant as a fallback, pricing for subsequent billing periods will reflect the pricing of the served variant."

- Proposed (redline):
  "If Redwood elects to route Customer traffic to a compatible model variant as a fallback for operational reasons (\"Fallback Event\"), the following shall apply:
   1) Preservation of Guaranteed Minimums: The Customer's committed floor(s) set forth in this Order Form shall remain in effect for the remainder of the applicable Commitment Period and shall not be reduced as a result of any Fallback Event, except as expressly agreed in writing.
   2) Notification and Approval Window: Redwood will provide Customer written notice of any Fallback Event that is reasonably expected to result in a proposed change to the pricing floor(s). Customer shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of such notice (the \"Review Period\") to accept or reject the proposed change in writing.
   3) Rejection Remedy / True-up: If Customer rejects a proposed floor reduction, Redwood will: (a) suspend any change to the floor pending remediation; and (b) provide an operational remediation plan to restore the original floor-level guarantees within thirty (30) calendar days. If Redwood is unable to restore the floor within the remediation period, Customer may elect either (i) a pro rata credit for the impacted period calculated against the original floor, or (ii) termination for convenience of the affected SKUs without further liability.
   4) Temporary Routing Pricing: For the duration of the Fallback Event, traffic served by the fallback variant will be priced at the serving-variant rate for invoicing purposes, provided that such temporary routing does not permanently rebaseline the Customer's committed floor(s).
   5) Materiality Threshold: A proposed floor reduction shall be deemed \"material\" only if the aggregate reduction exceeds ten percent (10%) of the Customer's committed annual floor; reductions below this threshold require notice but not the rejection remedy."

Comments:
- This preserves committed economics while allowing Redwood to operate resiliently.
- We intentionally separate temporary serving rates from contractual minima to avoid the snapshot rebaseline issue.
- We included the 10% materiality threshold to avoid operational churn for small rebaselines.

Please review and let me know if Acme's legal/procurement wants the remediation timeline shortened or different remedies. Karthik — if you'd like, I can convert this to tracked changes on the PDF and send a clean/marked version to Liam.
